newsitem.title: UK: NATWEST SAYS APPOINTED BY ROMANIA'S SIDEX.
newsitem.headline: NATWEST SAYS APPOINTED BY ROMANIA'S SIDEX.

text.p: UK investment bank NatWest Markets said on Tuesday it had been appointed by Romanian steel company Sidex SA to assist in raising international capital and advising the state-owned firm on its privatisation.

NatWest Markets, the investment banking arm of National Westminster Bank Plc, said in a statement Sidex ranks as one of Romania's largest companies and produces around 75 percent of the country's steel.
Sidex exports about 60 percent of its production -- representing around 15 percent of Romania's total exports -- and is one of Romania's "most important hard currency earners".
But a representative for the group said it needs to finance its working capital, describing this as the most important issue it currently faces.

"Despite its strong underlying business, in recent years Sidex has had to operate with inadequate working capital. Our first priority therefore will be to raise Sidex's short term finance, using various trade finance techniques," NatWest Markets said.

Sidex said the completion of the first phase of a modernisation programme, which had involved spending $240 million over the last three years, had "significantly enhanced Sidex's already positive competitive position".
NatWest said it would advise the company over the next few months "on their future privatisation strategy and the options available to them".
In March, Sidex said it planned to raise up to $200 million in Eurobonds through U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch and was seeking a $100 million loan.
Most of Sidex's 36,000 employees are based in Galati, east of Bucharest.
